questions.stem:
A group of 40 families was asked whether their family had a dog, a cat or a rabbit as pets.

No family had a dog and a rabbit
2 families had both a dog and a cat
12 families had a dog
14 families had a cat
11 families had a rabbit
9 families did not have any of these animals as pets

A family from this group is selected at random.

$D$ represents the event that the family has a dog
$C$ represents the event that the family has a cat
$R$ represents the event that the family has a rabbit

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to illustrate this information.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) B1: for 3 intersecting circles with $n(D \cap R) = 0$ (either diagram) [Blank is not equiv to 0]. B1: for a box and 9 outside the circles. B1: for $n(D \cap C) = 2$ and $n(D \cap C') = 10$. B1: for 8, 4 and 7 correctly placed. Allow probabilities (out of 40) or decimals or integers.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) State, giving a reason, a pair of mutually exclusive events from $D$, $C$ and $R$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: for $D$ and $R$ with a suitable reason (extra pairs is B0) e.g. $\mathrm{P}(D \cap R) = 0$ Condone $\varnothing$ for 0 or no intersection/overlap. Must see an attempt at a reason. Must be $D$, $R$ not $\mathrm{P}(D)$, $\mathrm{P}(R)$. $\mathrm{P}(D \cup R) = \mathrm{P}(D)+\mathrm{P}(R)$ is not a suitable reason though.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Since no family has a dog and a rabbit a mutually exclusive pair is $D$, $R$ B1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the probability that the family has exactly 2 of these kinds of animals as pets.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: For (c) onwards if their $N \neq 40$ allow denominators of probs with 40 or $N$. (c) B1ft: ft their "4" (but must give a proper fraction) ft blank as 0 or $\frac{3}{20}$ or exact equivalent. $\left[\frac{2+"4"}{40}\right] = \frac{3}{20}$

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Showing your working clearly, determine whether or not the events $D$ and $C$ are independent.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) M1: for stating all the probabilities (values) required for a suitable test, must be labelled. Must use $D$ and $C$ ft their VD. Must be clear which test they are trying to use. A1: for the correct probabilities and correct calculation or comparison and correct conclusion e.g. $\mathrm{P}(D \cap C) = \frac{2}{40} = \frac{1}{20}$ $\mathrm{P}(D) = \frac{12}{40} = \frac{3}{10}$ $\mathrm{P}(C) = \frac{14}{40} = \frac{7}{20}$ or $\frac{1}{20} \neq \frac{3}{10}\times\frac{7}{20} = \left[\frac{21}{200}\right]$ so they are not independent. ALT: $\mathrm{P}(C) = \frac{14}{40} = \frac{7}{20}$ vs $\mathrm{P}(C|D) = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}$ or $\mathrm{P}(D) = \frac{12}{40} = \frac{3}{10}$ vs $\mathrm{P}(D|C) = \frac{2}{14} = \frac{1}{7}$

parts.label: e
parts.text:
Sarah's family is in the group and her family has a pet cat.

(e) Find the probability that Sarah's family also has a pet rabbit.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (e) M1: for a correct ratio of probabilities (ft their 4): either as an expression or values $\left[\mathrm{P}(R|C) = \right]\frac{\mathrm{P}(R \cap C)}{\mathrm{P}(C)}$ or $\frac{"\frac{4}{40}"}{\frac{14}{40}}$ A1ft: for $\frac{2}{7}$ or exact equivalent (allow ft of their 4 [$\neq 0$] provided it gives an exact fraction) $= \frac{4}{14} = \frac{2}{7}$

parts.label: f
parts.text:
(f) Find the exact value of $\mathrm{P}([D \cup R] \mid C')$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (f) M1: for a correct ratio (possibly of probabilities) ft their 10 and their 7 [Not expression here] $\frac{"10"+"7"}{"10"+"7"+9}$ (o.e.) A1: for $\frac{17}{26}$ (accept $0.6\dot{5}3846\dot{1}$)

questions.notes:
MS shows a recurring decimal notation with a dot above the final digit for 17/26; transcribed as 0.653846 with a recurring dot over the last 1, matching the OCR reading.
[fix_parts] (f) mark_scheme: '0.653846\\dot{1}' -> '0.6\\dot{5}3846\\dot{1}' (MS p.5 prints 0.6538461 with recurring dots over the 5 and the 1 (17/26))

questions.stem: The random variable $X$ has a normal distribution with mean 10 and standard deviation 6

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: for standardising 7 (or 13) with 10 and 6 (allow $\pm$). M1: for $1-p$ (where $0.68<p<0.70$). A1: for awrt 0.309 (calc. 0.3085375......) (Ans only scores 3/3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\mathrm{P}(X<7) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{7-10}{6}\right) = \mathrm{P}(Z<-0.5)$ M1; $= 1-0.6915$ M1; $= 0.308537\ldots$ awrt $0.309$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the value of $k$ such that
$\mathrm{P}(10-k<X<10+k) = 0.60$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Standardising $10 \pm k$ with 10 and 6 and setting equal to $z$ value $0.8<|z|<0.9$. B1: for $z=\pm 0.8416$ or better (calc gives 0.8416212.....) used in a linear equation for $k$. A1: $k=5.05$ or better (or use of $z=0.84$ and answer of 5.04). Ans only awrt 5.04 scores M1B0A1. Ans only: Answer in the range 5.049 ~ 5.0499 scores M1B1A1 but answer only of 5.05 is M1B0A1
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\frac{10+k-10}{6} = 0.8416$ M1 B1; $k = 5.0496$ awrt $5.05$ A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A single observation $x$, of $X$, is to be taken.
A rectangle is drawn on a centimetre grid with vertices having coordinates $(0,0)$, $(x,0)$, $(x,x-3)$ and $(0,x-3)$

(c) Find the probability that the area of this rectangle is more than $40\,\mathrm{cm}^2$
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: for a suitable expression for the area of the rectangle (in $x$ or $X$) [$\Rightarrow$ by 2nd or 3rd M1]. M1: for a correct quadratic inequality (accept $x(x-3)>40$ [o.e.]). M1: for an attempt to solve their 3TQ to find critical values (allow =0) (e.g. factorise) Allow $(X+8)(X-5)$ or use of formula with $\leqslant 1$ sign error or $\left(X-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2-k-40$ ($k>0$). A1: for the correct critical values (cvs) of 8 and $-5$. M1: for solving their quadratic inequality - taking the "outside" region (ft their cvs) [P(..) not required]. M1: for standardising at least one of their values (with 10 and 6 correctly) (ft their cvs). dM1: for an attempt at both probabilities: one $\approx 0.006$ and one $>0.6$ and adding or for $1-q$ where $q=0.36$ or better; this mark is dependent on all the other 5 M marks being scored. A1: for answer in range [0.6355, 0.637] with clear attempt at both probabilities used (calc 0.636768…). Ans only: If 6th M1 is not explicitly seen then must have an answer awrt 0.636 or 0.637
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Area of rectangle is $X(X-3)$ M1; Need $X(X-3)>40$ M1; $X^2-3X-40>0 \Rightarrow (X-8)(X+5)>0$ M1; So critical values are 8 and $-5$ A1; Need $\mathrm{P}(X>8)+\mathrm{P}(X<-5)$ or $1-\mathrm{P}(-5<X<8)$ M1
- So $\mathrm{P}(Z>-0.33)+\mathrm{P}(Z<-2.5)$ M1; $= 0.6293+0.0062$ dM1; $= 0.6355$ $[0.6355 \sim 0.637]$ A1
